commitResults.messageTitle: Person class: Persist created, edited and viewed times
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts have no record of when they were added, changed or looked at,
so later features (sort by activity, follow-ups) have nothing to build
on.

Let's,
* add an immutable Activity class holding optional created, last edited
  and last viewed times
* give Person an Activity, a withActivity copy method and a
  hasSameDetails comparison that ignores activity
* save the times as optional ISO-8601 UTC strings in the JSON file, and
  load a missing time as absent so v1.3 files still load
* keep activity when edit and tag replace a person
* describe the stored format in the Developer Guide

Optional times keep unknown history absent instead of inventing dates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Model: Record contact add, edit and view activity
commitResults.messageBody:
Activity fields exist on Person but nothing sets them, so every time
stays absent.

Let's,
* give ModelManager a Clock and a now() that returns whole seconds
* add Model#editPerson as the single rule for last edited: it does
  nothing when the details are unchanged, and otherwise stores the new
  person with the target's activity and last edited set to now
* add Model#viewPerson to set last viewed and the viewed person
* record created time in AddCommand, and use editPerson in EditCommand
  and TagCommand and viewPerson in ViewCommand
* document the rule in the Developer Guide with a sequence diagram, and
  note in the User Guide that view records the last viewed time

Putting the rule in the model lets later commands (notes, star,
follow-up, photo) record edits without repeating the timestamp logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Activity: Match the agreed storage contract
commitResults.messageBody:
The agreed v1.4 specification asks for whole-second UTC times and an
error that names the bad field. The first version accepted fractions of
a second and offsets, and reported every bad time with one message.

Let's,
* accept only times written as 2026-10-17T04:12:33Z, and reject
  fractions, offsets, spaces, empty text, 24:00:00 and leap seconds
* report a bad time as Invalid contact data: '<field>' must be an
  ISO-8601 UTC timestamp., naming createdAt, lastEditedAt or
  lastViewedAt, and share the message pattern for later fields
* keep Activity times to whole seconds
* document on the Person constructors that existing contacts are copied
  with withActivity or the model edit operation
* update the Developer Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Person class: Add toBuilder and use Singapore time
commitResults.messageBody:
The agreed v1.4 specification asks #105 to own one copy API that keeps
every field, so later features do not rebuild a contact with an
incomplete constructor call and lose data. It also fixes display and
"today" to Asia/Singapore.

Let's,
* add Person#toBuilder and a Person.Builder seeded with every field,
  and make withActivity use it
* copy contacts with toBuilder in the edit and tag commands
* default the model clock to Asia/Singapore through
  Model.DISPLAY_ZONE
* use a local variable for the created-time copy in AddCommand and
  point setViewedPerson users to viewPerson
* describe both in the Developer Guide and document the activity time
  fields in the User Guide data file section

commitResults.messageTitle: LogicManager: Undo a command whose save failed
commitResults.messageBody:
The agreed specification says a failed save must leave the data as it
was. LogicManager ran the command and then saved, so a failed save left
the change (and its time stamp) in memory.

Let's,
* add Model#createSnapshot and Model#restore, with an opaque Snapshot of
  the contacts, the viewed contact and the visible-list filter
* take a snapshot before each command and restore it when saving fails,
  for both IO and permission errors
* show the created, last edited and last viewed times in the detail
  panel in Singapore time, with an em dash for unknown times
* document both in the Developer and User Guides

Undo history can extend the same snapshot later.

commitResults.messageTitle: JsonAdaptedPerson: Name the field for non-string times
commitResults.messageBody:
A createdAt, lastEditedAt or lastViewedAt value that is a JSON object,
array, number or boolean made Jackson fail while reading the file, so
the user got a generic error instead of the agreed field-specific one.

Let's,
* read the three times as Object and let parseTime reject anything
  that is not a string with the field-specific message
* add a JSON-level test for all three fields

This way the data file error always names the field that is wrong.

commitResults.messageTitle: ModelManager: Check the target on a no-op edit
commitResults.messageBody:
editPerson returned early when the new details matched the target, so
a missing or stale target was accepted silently, although the Model
API says the target must exist and a real edit throws for it.

Let's,
* throw PersonNotFoundException before the no-op return when the
  target is not in the address book
* add a test for a no-op edit of a missing target

This way a no-op edit follows the same contract as any other edit.

The detail panel put its fields and the new CREATED, LAST EDITED and
LAST VIEWED rows in a VBox with no scrolling, so the bottom rows could
not be reached when the panel was short or the content grew. The #103
agreement requires a vertically scrolling detail panel.

Let's,
* wrap the details in a ScrollPane that fits the width and never shows
  a horizontal bar
* look inside the ScrollPane in the panel and main window tests, since
  lookup does not reach its content before it has a skin
* add a test for the scrolling settings

This way every row stays reachable at any window height.

commitResults.messageTitle: PersonDetailPanel: Keep the scroll area dark
commitResults.messageBody:

Let's,
* give the ScrollPane a detail-scroll style class
* make it and its viewport transparent in DarkTheme.css, and drop the
  inline style that only covered the ScrollPane itself

This way the panel keeps the dark theme and the text stays readable.

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Follow-up tests: Cover Singapore midnight and leap dates
commitResults.messageBody:
Follow-up and activity behaviour is tested one class at a time. Nothing
runs `followup` and `due` through LogicManager with real storage, and
the Singapore midnight, 29 Feb and malformed date or time cases are
only partly covered.

Let's,

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Document follow-up and due errors and messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The `followup` section has no error table and no success messages,
and the `due` section lacks the exact result message. The data file
section says LarperBoard "reports" an invalid time or date, but the
message only goes to the log and the app starts with an empty list.

Let's,
* restructure `followup` into format, rules, examples and an error
  table with the exact messages checked against the parser and command
* add the success and unchanged messages and the case-insensitive
  `clear` rule
* state the exact `due` result message, that it replaces filters, and
  that text after `due` is ignored
* say that invalid time and date values are written to the log
* describe the `followUpDate` field in the data file section

The guide must match what the app prints so that users and testers can
rely on it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test utilities: Share one MutableClock across tests

repeated in the others.

Let's,
* add testutil/MutableClock with Javadoc on every public member
* keep both advanceMillis and advanceSeconds, since the copies differed
* delete the four private copies and their unused java.time imports

One shared class removes the duplication without changing any test's
behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Contact card: Show tags on one row with +N overflow
commitResults.messageBody:
Cards wrap their tags onto extra rows, so a contact with many or long
tags makes its card taller than the rest, against the agreed v1.4
specification of one tag row with +N overflow.

Let's,
* replace the card's FlowPane of tags with a single non-wrapping HBox
* add TagRow, which shows the tags that fit the row's width and ends
  with a +N label for the hidden ones, refitting when the width changes
* keep the arithmetic in the pure TagRow#visibleTagCount so it can be
  tested without JavaFX
* style the +N label in a muted colour with the tag-overflow class
* leave the detail panel alone so it still shows every tag

Cards keep a uniform height, and the detail panel still lets the user
read all tags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Card tags: Measure +N for the tags actually hidden
commitResults.messageBody:
TagRow reserves the width of "+total" for the overflow label, but the
label shows "+hidden", which can be one digit shorter. With ten tags,
nine tags and "+1" can fit while nine tags and "+10" cannot, so a tag
is hidden that would have fit.

Let's,
* let visibleTagCount take the +N width as a function of hidden tags
* measure "+hidden" for each candidate in fit()
* test the boundary with ten tags, purely and on a styled card
* load DarkTheme.css in PersonCardTest so cards are measured as shown
* say in the DG that +N is measured for the hidden count

The row now shows every tag that fits next to its real count.

commitResults.messageTitle: Card tags: Place TagRow.fill after the constructor

commitResults.messageTitle: Card tags: Measure tags in whole pixels
commitResults.messageBody:
TagRow.fit() adds up the raw fractional preferred widths of the tags,
but the HBox lays each label out at a width rounded up to a whole pixel.
When the raw sum fits and the rounded sum does not, a label is squeezed
and shows "..." instead of its text.

Let's,
* measure each tag and the +N label with snapSizeX, and the gap with
  snapSpaceX, so fit() counts what the row will really lay out
* make the sweep test in PersonCardTest round the same way, step the
  width by a quarter pixel, and assert no shown label is squeezed
* mention the whole-pixel measuring in the Developer Guide

Measuring the way the layout rounds keeps the fit decision and the
rendered row in agreement at every width and display scale.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Explain meeting, followup, due and find
commitResults.messageBody:
New users cannot tell `meeting`, `followup` and `due` apart because
they are never described side by side, and `meeting` starts straight
with its syntax. `d/` (follow-up date) and `md/` (meeting date) are
easy to mix up, and it is not clear which prefixes belong to which
command. Plain `find Han` does not match `Hans Gruber` but typed
`find n/Han` does, and the guide does not point this out.

Let's,

* add a one-sentence purpose to the `meeting` section.
* add a table that compares `meeting`, `followup` and `due`.
* add a table that compares plain and typed `find`.
* add a prefix cheat sheet after the command summary.

This helps users pick the right command and prefix without reading
every section.

Fixes #231

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Tighten find and prefix cheat sheet wording
commitResults.messageBody:
The prefix cheat sheet says every other prefix makes find fail, but
find only rejects one when it starts a word, so text such as
`nt/x:p/1` is still accepted. The find comparison table also leaves
the photo out of what cannot be searched, and its header row uses a
different separator style from every other table in the guide.

Let's,

* say the reserved prefixes are rejected when they start a word, and
  link to the find section for the full rules.
* add the photo to the "Cannot search" row.
* use header-width dashes in the find table separator.

This keeps the guide exact about what find accepts.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Clarify detail panel after due list edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The due section said "for any other contact it stays as it is", which
can be read as any other contact in the panel.

Let's,
* say what happens when the viewed contact leaves the due list and
  what happens when a different contact is being viewed

The reviewer's wording is clearer for the reader.
Simplify follow-up date and no-op messages
Align follow-up docs and add user-story status

commitResults.messageTitle: MainWindow: Close Help whenever the main window hides
commitResults.messageBody:
Help is only closed by handleExit(), which runs on a close request.
If the main window is hidden any other way, such as Stage#close(), the
close request is skipped and the Help window stays open, keeping
LarperBoard running.

Let's,

* listen for WINDOW_HIDDEN on the primary stage and hide Help there.
* add a package-private MainWindow constructor that takes a HelpWindow.
* add tests for the close request and for hiding without one.

Help should never outlive the main window, however it is closed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add manual test for closing with Help open
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual tests for launch and shutdown do not cover closing the main
window while the Help window is open.

Let's,

* add a test case that closes the main window with Help showing.

This is the case reported in #242, so testers can check it by hand.
User Guide: explain meeting vs followup vs due, the d/ and md/ prefixes, and the two find forms

commitResults.messageTitle: MainWindowTest: Check Help in the existing close test
commitResults.messageBody:
closeRequest_closesHelpWindow repeats the setup and assertions of
closeRequest_withoutExitCommand_closesAtOnce, and the Help checks
accept any number of hides.

Let's,

* check that Help is hidden in the existing close-request test, and
  drop the duplicate test.
* expect exactly one hide, and no saved window settings when the
  window is hidden without a close request.
* use the default HelpWindow constructor in RecordingHelpWindow.

This keeps the tests free of duplication and pins that only a close
request saves the window settings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Scope the Help manual test to user exits
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual test for closing with Help open reads as a check of the
#242 fix, but the title-bar close already closed Help before it, so
the test passes either way.

Let's,

* name the case after what it checks, the user-facing exits.
* add File > Exit and the exit command to the steps.
* say that hiding the window without a close request is covered by
  MainWindowTest, as it cannot be done by hand.

Testers should not take this case as proof of the fix.
Closing the main window leaves Help open and LarperBoard running

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Relaunch between Help exit tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The Help exit manual test closes the app in its first step, so the
File > Exit and exit command steps cannot be followed as written.

Let's,
* tell testers to relaunch the app and reopen Help before each step

This keeps each exit path testable on its own.
Developer Guide: Relaunch the app between Help exit manual tests

commitResults.messageTitle: About Us: Add Cheryl's details and photo
commitResults.messageBody:
The About Us page still shows a template entry for this team
member, with a placeholder photo and placeholder links.

Replace it with Cheryl's name, profile photo and GitHub link. The

About Us: Update Cheryl's responsibilities

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add LarperBoard glossary terms
commitResults.messageBody:
The glossary only contains two terms inherited from AddressBook,
one of which is not used anywhere in the Developer Guide, so readers
have no definitions for the terms specific to LarperBoard.

Replace the unused term and define the terms used in the user stories
and use cases, such as contact, tag, note, archive and export, so the
guide is understandable without prior knowledge of the product.
Developer Guide: Add LarperBoard glossary terms

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Refine target user and value proposition
commitResults.messageBody:
The target user profile and value proposition do not yet mention
that users find saving contacts on a phone too much effort during an
event, forget many contacts afterwards, or may have unreliable
internet at crowded venues.

Add these points so that the profile matches the persona and the
user stories, and rewrite the value proposition to lead with the
outcome and mention that data is stored locally.
Developer Guide: Refine target user and value proposition

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to show a person's details
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can only see a compact summary of each person in the list,
and there is no command to look at a single person on its own.

Add the view command, which takes the index of a person in the
displayed list and shows that person's details in the result
display. An invalid index is rejected in the same way as for the
delete command. The detail panel will be added in a later change.
Add view command

The view command reports a generic format error when the user gives
more than one index or an index larger than the integer limit, and
reports an invalid index when the person list is empty. The delete
command already reports each of these cases specifically.

Show the same specific messages as the delete command for multiple
indexes and for an oversized index, and show that the person list is
empty when there is nobody to view.
Handle view command edge cases

commitResults.messageTitle: Add detail panel for the view command
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command shows the viewed person as a single line of text in
the result display.

This is hard to read when a person has many tags, and it disappears as
soon as the next command is run.

Let's add a detail panel next to the person list that shows the name,
phone, email, LinkedIn handle and tags of the viewed person, and shows
that no contact is selected until a person is viewed.

The model keeps track of the viewed person so that the panel can follow
it without the UI having to know about the view command. The minimum
window width is raised from 450 to 700 to fit the panel.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add LogicManager tests for the viewed person
commitResults.messageBody:
The LogicManager method that exposes the viewed person to the UI is
not exercised by any test.

Add tests that check that no person is viewed at the start and that
the viewed person is the one selected by the view command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add MainWindow test for the detail panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The code that adds the detail panel to the main window is not
exercised by any test, so a mistake in how the panel is wired up
would go unnoticed.

Add a test that builds the main window and checks that the detail panel
is part of it and shows the person selected by the view command.
Add detail panel for the view command

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep detail panel in sync with the contact list
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel keeps showing the viewed person after that person
has been edited, tagged or deleted, or after the address book has been
cleared, so it can show details that are out of date or no longer exist.

Let's make the model update the viewed person whenever it replaces or
removes that person, and clear it when all data is replaced, so the
panel shows the updated contact or goes back to showing that no contact
is selected.

The default window is 740 by 600, which is too small now that the
main window shows the person list and the detail panel side by side.

Change the default to 900 by 720, so that the person list keeps its
width and the detail panel has room for the details of a contact.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Add view command section
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not describe the view command or the detail panel
that it fills, so users cannot find out how to see all the details of
a person.

Add a section for view with its format, what the detail panel shows,
examples and the error messages, together with a screenshot of the
panel, and add view to the command summary.
Keep detail panel in sync with the contact list
Enlarge default window size
User Guide: Add view command section

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command history to the command box
commitResults.messageBody:
Users have to retype a command to run it again or to fix a typo,
which is slow when they enter many commands in a row.

Let's keep the latest 50 submitted commands in memory, including
commands that fail, and bring them back with the Up and Down arrows
while the command box has focus. The text typed before browsing started
is restored after the newest command. Modified key presses and arrow
keys in other controls are left alone. The history is not saved to the
data file. The controls are described in the User Guide.

Some branches in the command history code can never be taken or are
never tested, such as the shortcut-key check that repeats the control
and meta checks.

Remove the redundant shortcut-key check, keep a single assertion for the
history position, and add a test that other keys are not intercepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note class: Add optional note to contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts have no place for free-form remarks, such as where the
person was met or what to follow up on.

Let's add an optional Note of at most 1000 characters to Person and
carry it through Person.Builder, so that copies made with toBuilder keep
it. The note is saved as a note string in the data file. A missing note
loads as no note, so older files still load, and a blank, too long or
non-string note makes the file invalid with a message naming the field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command to set and clear a note
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot change the note of a contact once the Note field exists.

Add note INDEX nt/TEXT to set or replace a note and note INDEX clear to
remove it. Blank and too long notes are rejected with their own
messages. Setting the same note again, or clearing a missing note,
changes nothing and does not update the last edited time. The command
copies the contact with toBuilder and Model#editPerson, so the other
details and the activity times are kept.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detail panel: Show the note and scroll
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel does not show the note of a contact, and it cannot
show more than fits on the screen.

Let's show the full note below the tags, wrapped to the width of the
panel, and put the details in a scroll pane that scrolls vertically
only, so that a long note can be read without a second scroll bar or
text running off the side.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The User Guide and Developer Guide do not describe notes.

Add the note command, its error messages and the note field of the data
file to the User Guide, and describe the Note field and its storage in
the Developer Guide.

The note command parser parses the index in two separate return
statements, one of which is longer than the line limit.

Work out which form was typed first, reject the other shapes with the
format error, then parse the index once and build the command in one
place. The order of the errors stays the same: a wrong shape is still
reported before a bad index, which a new test checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep note text out of the logs and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The text of a note is personal, but it could be written to the log
through the logged command, through Person.toString when the address
book is logged at startup, and through the error log of the main window.
The data file also accepted an empty note, which the User Guide says is
invalid.

Hide the arguments of a note command wherever a command is logged, and
show only the length of a note in toString. Reject an empty note string
in the data file, because a person without a note is saved as null.
Add tests that capture the log output and check the note text is not in
it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the log of a failed command in the window
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window logs a command when it fails, but no test makes a
command fail through the window, so that line never runs in the tests
and it is not checked that a note command is logged without its text.

Add a test that fails a note command through the command box and checks
that the log has the hidden command and not the text of the note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use plain line endings in MainWindowTest
commitResults.messageBody:
The previous commit stored MainWindowTest with Windows line endings,
which the repository check rejects, so the Ubuntu job failed and the
other jobs were cancelled.

Convert the file back to plain line endings, as in the rest of the
repository.
Add freeform notes to contacts

commitResults.messageTitle: Add starred flag to Person and storage
commitResults.messageBody: Persons can now be marked as important. The flag defaults to false and is saved as an optional starred boolean, so older data files still load. A value that is not true or false is rejected with a field-specific message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add star, unstar and filter commands
commitResults.messageBody: star and unstar set the flag through Model#editPerson, so changes are saved and can be undone. Repeating the current state is a no-op with a message. filter starred shows only starred contacts and filter starred off shows everyone. Both commands log at INFO without personal details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a star next to starred contacts
commitResults.messageBody: Starred contacts get a star beside their name in the list and in the detail panel, so important contacts stand out at a glance. The label is hidden and takes no space when the contact is not starred.
Add the commands, the starred data field and the design notes to the user guide and developer guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move star to top right of contact card
commitResults.messageBody: The star sat next to the name and could be pushed off long names. Pin it to the top right corner of the card instead so starred contacts are easy to spot.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move detail panel star to the top right
commitResults.messageBody: Match the contact card by pinning the star to the top right corner of the detail panel. It is hidden when no contact is selected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clear selection when a star change hides it
commitResults.messageBody: filter starred left the viewed contact in the detail panel after the list stopped showing it, and unstar did the same when the contact left a starred filter. Clear the selection in both commands, but only for the edited contact in unstar so unrelated selections are kept. find keeps its existing behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align star docs with the card layout
commitResults.messageBody: The user guide and developer guide said the star sits next to the name, but it is drawn in the top right corner. Describe the real position, and mark the filter replacement behaviour with a TODO for the combined filters in #128.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test star card cue, undo and reload
commitResults.messageBody: Check that the card shows and manages the star only for starred people, that undo brings back the flag and activity times, and that a starred contact is saved and read back through the JSON storage.
Show how star and unstar move from the parser through Model#editPerson to the selection check, for the developer guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop outdated lifeline note from star diagram
commitResults.messageBody: The hidden arrow makes the StarCommandParser lifeline stop at the destroy marker, so the PlantUML limitation note no longer applies.
Add star, unstar and filter commands

commitResults.messageTitle: Document command history in the guides
commitResults.messageBody: Add the Up/Down recall to the user guide command summary and describe the CommandHistory and CommandBox design in the developer guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention reset in the command history guide
commitResults.messageBody: reset does not clear the command history and is remembered like any other command, so list it with list and clear.
Add command history to the command box

The view, note and star parsers each repeated the same try/catch that turns a bad index into the displayed-index message, so move it to ParserUtil#parseDisplayedIndex. The view and delete parsers also defined the same multiple-index message, so keep one copy in Messages. No behaviour changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share the model copy helper in command tests
commitResults.messageBody: NoteCommandTest and StarCommandTest each had their own copy of the same copyOf helper, so move it to CommandTestUtil.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove unused detail panel style class
commitResults.messageBody: No stylesheet or test uses the detail-panel style class on the panel root.

commitResults.messageTitle: Scroll the detail panel by wheel pixels
commitResults.messageBody: JavaFX scrolls the panel by the wheel amount as a fraction of the whole content height instead of the scrollable part, so it needed many flicks to reach the bottom. Scroll by the real pixel amount instead, clamped to the top and bottom.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the detail panel scroll handler
commitResults.messageBody: Fire real scroll events at the panel to check that it scrolls by the pixels of the event, handles the event itself, and leaves content that fits in place. The UI tests do not run on the Linux CI runner, but they do on macOS and Windows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move scroll decision into the tested method
commitResults.messageBody: Only the scroll position calculation could be covered on CI, which skips JavaFX UI tests. Move the checks for a zero scroll and for content that fits into that method so the handler is a single statement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the clock used by the copyOf test helper
commitResults.messageBody: copyOf builds the copy with FIXED_CLOCK and fresh UserPrefs, so say so in its Javadoc to avoid confusing failures when it is used with a model that has another clock.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review comments on the scroll handler
commitResults.messageBody: Measure the content with its layout bounds in both the handler and the test, as ScrollPane does, assert the 0 to 1 scroll range, make the handler easier to read, and check in the content-fits test that the event is left alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the scroll pane range instead of asserting it
commitResults.messageBody: The assertion for a 0 to 1 scroll range left a branch that no test can take. Pass the pane's vmin and vmax to the scroll calculation instead, so it does not depend on the default range and there is nothing to assert.
Turn assertions on explicitly for the test and run tasks so the team repo has them enabled in build.gradle, as the course checklist requires.
Remove redundant code in view, note and star parts
Scroll the detail panel by wheel pixels
Enable assertions in the build

commitResults.messageTitle: List available commands for an unknown command
commitResults.messageBody: A typo such as strar 1 only said Unknown command, so list every command word in the message. The list lives in AddressBookParser#COMMAND_WORDS, and a test scans the command classes so that a new command word cannot be forgotten.
Describe the list of available commands in the user guide, and how COMMAND_WORDS is kept complete in the developer guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long messages in the result box
commitResults.messageBody: The unknown command message lists every command word and ran off the side of the result box with a horizontal scroll bar. Turn on text wrapping so long messages are readable without scrolling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the contact photo beside the name in the detail panel
commitResults.messageBody: Remove the photo and the No photo placeholder from the list cards. In the detail panel, show the photo to the right of the name in a fixed 160x120 frame so photos of different shapes and the placeholder take the same space.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the new photo layout in the guides
commitResults.messageBody: The photo is now shown only in the detail panel, beside the name, in a fixed frame.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review comments on unknown command list

Shorten the user guide example so that it does not go stale each time
a command is added or removed. Explain the fully qualified assertThrows
in the parser test, and give the test helpers verb names as the coding
standard asks.

Add a manual testing entry to the developer guide, and a layout test
that the command list fits the result pane at the minimum window width.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move the photo below a long name in a narrow panel
commitResults.messageBody:
At the minimum window width the detail panel is about 360 pixels wide,
and the photo left only a narrow column for the name, so a long name
became very tall and pushed the other details down. Show the photo under
the name when the header is narrower than 400 pixels.

Check the layout at the narrow width and at a wide width, with and
without a loaded photo, in the tests.

commitResults.messageBody:

cards. Describe the narrow panel layout in both guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix usage message when clear comes first
commitResults.messageBody:
The photo, meeting and followup parsers took the first word as the
index, so "photo clear" and "photo clear 1" reported an invalid index
instead of the usage. Report the usage when the first word is clear, in
any letter case, and keep the invalid index message for a wrong index
before clear.

Add parser tests for the three commands, including the cases that must
keep their messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Count note length in characters, not UTF-16 units
commitResults.messageBody:
The limit of 1000 characters on a note used String#length, which counts
an emoji as two, so 501 emoji were rejected as too long, and a data file
with such a note failed to load. Count code points instead, in one
place used by the note, the parser, the storage and the log text.

Add tests for emoji at the limit in the model, the parser, the command
parser and the JSON storage, and say in the guides what counts as one
character.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a dash for a contact with no tags
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel left an empty gap after the TAGS heading for a contact
without tags, while every other missing field shows a dash. Show a dash
in its own label in place of the tag row, because the tag row styles
every label inside it like a tag.

Check in the tests that the dash and the tag row take turns as the
viewed contact changes.
149 List available commands for an unknown command
176 Show a dash for a contact with no tags

commitResults.messageTitle: Check clear before duplicate photo prefixes
commitResults.messageBody:
photo clear f/a.png f/b.png reported a duplicate f/ prefix instead of the usage, because the duplicate check ran before the clear guard. Run the guard first so clear in the index position always reports the usage, and keep the duplicate prefix error for a valid index.

Add regression tests for both orderings.

The Javadoc said the limit is what the user sees, which is broader than the implementation: a flag or a letter with a combining accent displays as one symbol but counts as several code points. Say that it counts Unicode code points and not UTF-16 chars.
151 Show contact photo beside the name in the view panel only

commitResults.messageTitle: Share one emoji constant across note tests
commitResults.messageBody: The U+1F600 string was built separately in five places across four test classes. Define it once as TypicalNotes.EMOJI and use it in all of them.
Count note length in characters, not UTF-16 units

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept clear in any letter case after the index
commitResults.messageBody:
photo 1 CLEAR and meeting 1 CLEAR gave the usage error while followup 1 CLEAR worked, because only followup compared case-insensitively. Use ParserUtil.isClearKeyword for the word after the index in all three parsers, so there is one definition of clear.

Add tests for photo 1 CLEAR and meeting 1 CLEAR.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept the meeting clear field in any case
commitResults.messageBody:
meeting 1 CLEAR date worked but meeting 1 clear DATE gave the usage error, because the field name was matched case-sensitively. Lowercase the field name before checking it and pass the lowercase value to MeetingCommand.

Add tests that every spelling clears only the named field.

# Conflicts:
#	src/test/java/seedu/address/logic/parser/ParserUtilTest.java
photo, meeting and followup report an invalid index when clear comes first

commitResults.messageTitle: Shorten note, star and filter format errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Wrong-format errors for note, star, unstar and filter printed the whole
command description, parameter list and examples, about 560 characters
for note. The result box is 100 px high, so the part that says what to
fix could be below the fold, and every mistake got the same text.

Keep the Invalid command format! heading and follow it with one short
hint that fits the mistake:
- note: a missing index, a missing note or clear, text without nt/,
  too many words, and nt/ together with clear each get their own hint
- star and unstar: a missing index and extra words get their own hint
  that names the command
- filter: nothing typed and a wrong word get their own hint

Validation, the other messages and the shared index, empty-list and
duplicate-field wording are unchanged. Update the tests to expect the
new hints, and the note error table in the User Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reword the note error for extra parameters
commitResults.messageBody:
The note error for extra arguments says "Too many words", but the extra
argument can be a second index or text after clear, so it is a
parameter and not a word. The User Guide and the shared message "Only
one index parameter is accepted." both call it a parameter.

Say "Too many parameters", so that the same thing has the same name in
every message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Pause briefly before closing on exit
commitResults.messageBody:
After the exit command, the result box shows "Exiting Address Book as
requested ..." but the window closes in the same moment, so the message
cannot be read.

Keep the window open for one second after a typed exit command, and
ignore input in the command box meanwhile, so that the message can be
read. The Exit menu item and the close button of the window still close
it at once, because the user has already chosen to leave.
Pause briefly before exiting so the exit message can be read

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that format errors fit the result box
commitResults.messageBody:
The note hint test says the hints fit on one line, but it only checks
that each hint is at most 70 characters. How the text wraps depends on
the width and font of the result box, so the character count does not
show that no scrolling is needed.

Check the complete wrong-format messages of note, star, unstar and
filter in the result box at the minimum window width, and fail if a
scroll bar appears. Keep the character budget as a guard against long
hints, and name the test for what it checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ask for the INDEX when note has only clear
commitResults.messageBody:
For "note clear", the hint says "Add nt/NOTE, or use: note INDEX
clear.", but the user has already given the operation. What is missing
is the INDEX.

Treat a lone clear, in any letter case, as a missing index and show the
hint that asks for it. The other wrong forms keep their own hints.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test a note with more than two words before it
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov reports one partly covered branch in NoteCommandParser. The
check for a note given together with clear is only tested with exactly
two words before the nt/ prefix, so a note with three or more words
before it is never tested.

Add tests for more than two words before nt/, with and without clear as
the second word, which give the too many parameters hint.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop the exit tests opening real windows
commitResults.messageBody:
The macOS CI job has crashed with exit value 134 since the exit tests
were added to MainWindowTest. They open real windows with show() and
turn off the JavaFX implicit exit so that closing a window does not stop
the toolkit. Opening a window is the likely cause, because no other
test does it and the macOS job passed before they were added.

Run the same checks without showing a window. The window settings are
saved just before the window is hidden, so count those saves to see that
the window closes after the pause, only once, and at once for the close
button. Drop the implicit exit setup, which nothing needs now.
Exit tests crash the macOS CI runner
Simplify note, starred-contact, and command-entry error messages

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify the purpose of note, star, filter and help
commitResults.messageBody:
Several command sections opened with a format line and a dense list of
rules, so a reader could not tell what a command is for or what it
prints. The star and filter sections also listed no error messages
that the note section already had.

State the purpose of help, note, star, unstar, filter, exit and
command recall first, then the format, the rules and a table of the
result messages. Add error tables for star and filter. Explain that
help only shows the guide's address, that recall is not Tab
completion, and that undo and recall history clear on exit. Add the
Up and F1 shortcuts to the Quick start and the command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align the Developer Guide with note, star and help
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide said the help command displays instructions for
every command, but the help window only shows the address of the
online User Guide. It also said no feature needs an internet
connection, and it had no use cases or manual tests for notes, stars,
the starred filter, command recall or exit.

Correct the help use case and qualify the offline requirement. Add
use cases for the missing commands, describe the help window, command
history and exit pause in the UI section, update the glossary and add
manual test cases for each command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept command words in any letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
Command words such as list and star only worked in lower case. HELP
or STAR 1 gave Unknown command, which does not say that the letter
case is the problem, while keywords inside commands such as clear
and starred already ignored case.

Lower-case the command word before choosing a command, so that every
command works in any letter case. Compare the command word without
regard to case in the log redactor too, so that NOTE and FIND are
still kept out of the log. Say in the User Guide that command words
are not case-sensitive.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the active filter when adding a contact
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding a contact reset an active find, group or filter starred to
show every contact, so the list and heading changed without the user
asking. Other commands that change a contact, such as edit, tag and
star, keep the filter and update its count.

Stop the model from resetting the filter when a contact is added. The
new contact is listed only if it matches the filter, and list shows
every contact. Say so in the User Guide and the Developer Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align command-word docs and redaction with the parser
commitResults.messageBody:
The sort section said the command word remains lowercase, which is
no longer true now that command words ignore letter case. The
Developer Guide also did not say that the parser lower-cases the
command word, and the log redactor compared words in a different way
from the parser, with a condition that was easy to misread.

Remove the outdated sentence, describe the lower-casing in the
Developer Guide, and make the log redactor lower-case with
Locale.ROOT exactly as the parser does so that every spelling the
parser accepts is redacted. Bracket the find condition and use
Locale.ROOT in the test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow hyphens and apostrophes in names
commitResults.messageBody:

could only contain letters, digits and spaces, so many real names
could not be added or edited.

Accept hyphens and apostrophes inside a name. A name must still start
with a letter or digit, stay within 50 characters and use English
letters. Say in the User Guide which characters are allowed and that
a hyphenated name counts as one word for a plain find.
